questions.question: Indian Space Policy, 2023 sets the stage for _________ participation in space industry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__private sector__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Space Policy, 2023 sets the stage for private sector participation in the space industry.
 
• The policy aims to encourage and institutionalize private sector participation in the space sector's value chain, including the creation of space and ground-based assets. 
 
• The policy also allows Indian customers to directly procure space technology and services from public and private sources.
 
• It also gives non-governmental entities (NGEs) the ability to file with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and engage in commercial recovery of asteroid resources. 
 
• The policy's goal is to unlock the potential of India's youth and entrepreneurs by promoting private sector activity in high-technology areas, including space. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Public sector
 
• Owned and controlled by the government, with the goal of providing goods and services to the public at a reasonable cost. Public sector organizations include government agencies, state-owned enterprises, and municipalities. 
 
• Private sector
 
• Owned and operated by individuals or private groups, with the goal of making a profit. Private sector industries include manufacturing, technology, healthcare, and retail. 
 
• Joint sector
 
• Owned by both the government and private individuals, also known as public-private partnerships. Joint sector companies are an extension of the mixed economy concept, where both public and private enterprises work together to contribute to economic development.

questions.question: This famous classical dancer and choreographer is known for popularizing the Odissi dance form and founding the Nrityagram dance village. Who is she?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protima Gauri**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Protima Gauri was a famous classical dancer and choreographer who played a pivotal role in popularizing the Odissi dance form.
 
• She is also known for founding Nrityagram, a dance village in India dedicated to the preservation and promotion of classical dance forms, particularly Odissi.
 
• Nrityagram has become an iconic centre for classical dance training and performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sonal Mansingh
 
• Sonal Mansingh is a renowned Indian classical dancer and one of the leading exponents of Odissi and Bharatanatyam dance forms. She is celebrated for her grace, expressive style, and mastery of these classical traditions. Although she is a prominent figure in Indian classical dance, she is not associated with founding Nrityagram. Sonal Mansingh has contributed significantly to the popularization and preservation of Odissi, but her work is distinct from Protima Gauri's creation of Nrityagram.
 
• Rukmini Devi Arundale
 
• Rukmini Devi Arundale was a pioneering Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and theosophist who is best known for reviving Bharatanatyam, which was in danger of fading due to its association with temple dancing. She played a crucial role in shaping modern Bharatanatyam and founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai, a renowned institution for training in Indian classical dance and arts. While Rukmini Devi Arundale made invaluable contributions to Indian dance, she is not connected to Odissi or the founding of Nrityagram.
 
• Sanjukta Panigrahi
 
• Sanjukta Panigrahi was an iconic Odissi dancer and one of the most prominent figures in the revival and popularization of the Odissi dance form in modern times. She was known for her classical Odissi performances and her efforts to bring the art form into the mainstream. However, Sanjukta Panigrahi did not found Nrityagram; that was the achievement of Protima Gauri.

questions.question: _______, (born c. 350 BC-died c. 290), ancient Greek historian and diplomat, is author of Indica.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Megasthenes was an ancient Greek historian and diplomat who is best known for his work *Indica*, which provided an account of India and its people based on his observations during his time as an ambassador in the Maurya Empire.
 
• Megasthenes (c. 350 BC - c. 290 BC) was a Greek historian and diplomat who served as an ambassador to the Maurya Empire during the reign of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (the founder of the Maurya dynasty).
 
• He was sent to India by Seleucus I, one of Alexander the Great's generals who later founded the Seleucid Empire.
 
• Megasthenes is most famous for his work *Indica*, which he wrote based on his experiences and observations during his stay at the Mauryan court in Pataliputra (modern-day Patna).
 
• In *Indica*, he described various aspects of Indian society, culture, geography, and the political system under Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• While his account was not purely historical, it provided valuable insights into the life of ancient India and was an important source for later Greek historians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Xuanzang**: A Chinese Buddhist monk who traveled to India in the 7th century and wrote a detailed account of his journey, but lived centuries after Megasthenes.
 
• **James Legge**: A Scottish sinologist and missionary, primarily known for his translations of Chinese texts, not involved with India.
 
• **Seleucus I**: A Greek general and founder of the Seleucid Empire who sent Megasthenes as an ambassador to India, but did not write *Indica*.

questions.question: In any tennis game, first point is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In tennis, the points in a game are counted as 15, 30, 40, and then game point.
 
• The first point in a game is referred to as **15**.
 
• **0 points** = Love
 
• **1 point** = 15
 
• **2 points** = 30
 
• **3 points** = 40
 
• **4 points** = Game point (if the player has a 2-point lead)
 
• To win a game, a player must win four points by a margin of at least two points.
 
• When both players have 40 points, it's called "deuce". T
 
• o win the game, one player must win two consecutive points after the score reaches deuce. 
 
• Here are some other things to know about tennis:
 
• The first point of a game is served from the server's right side. 
 
• The server alternates serving from the right and left sides of their court from point to point. 
 
• The winner of a set is the first player to win six games, but they must also win by at least two games. 
 
• The winner of the match is determined by the outcome of a series of sets, which can be best of three or five sets. 
 
• The term "break point" refers to when the receiver has a chance to win the game with the next point.

questions.question: ________ founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiba Phule**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873.
 
• The organization's aim was to promote social equality, educate people, and fight against caste discrimination, especially the oppression faced by lower-caste communities in India.
 
• The Satyashodhak Samaj, which he founded in 1873, was a critical part of his mission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Debendra Nath Tagore (1817–1905)
 
 
• Debendra Nath Tagore was a prominent philosopher, religious reformer, and founder of the Brahmo Samaj, a reformist Hindu religious and social organization.
 
• Contributions:
 
• He is often referred to as the "father of the Brahmo Samaj" because of his pivotal role in the development and reform of the organization, which was established in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• Debendra Nath Tagore focused on rationalism and monotheism in religion, encouraging the worship of one God and the rejection of idol worship and outdated rituals.
 
• He emphasized the importance of social reforms, such as female education and abolition of Sati (the practice of widow immolation), which were central to the Brahmo Samaj's agenda.
 
• He also contributed to philosophical writing and intellectual discussions of the time, helping shape the religious and social reform movement in Bengal.
 
 
 
• Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang (Unknown, but primarily associated with the social and educational reforms in Maharashtra)
 
 
• Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang was a social reformer from Maharashtra known for his work on uplifting the marginalized sections of society. His focus was more on promoting education and social equality, especially for the lower castes and women.
 
• Contributions:
 
• He was a proponent of social equality and education, particularly for the people who were traditionally deprived of these opportunities due to caste-based discrimination.
 
• Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang was also active in the Brahmo Samaj and the Prarthana Samaj, which were reformist organizations aimed at social and religious reform, and often worked together with other reformers of the time like Maharshi Karve and M.G. Ranade.
 
• His work contributed to the broader reformist movement that sought to integrate the untouchables into mainstream society through education and social justice.
 
 
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901)
 
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade was a social reformer, judicial official, and academic who played a key role in the development of modern Indian thought.
 
• He was a prominent member of the Prarthana Samaj, a social and religious reform movement.
 
• Contributions:
 
• Ranade was deeply involved in promoting social reforms related to education, women’s rights, and economic development.
 
• He was an advocate for widow remarriage, abolition of child marriage, and education for girls.
 
• Ranade’s reforms were focused on improving the status of women and untouchables, promoting economic modernization, and scientific thinking.
 
• He was also involved in establishing educational institutions and was a key figure in the Indian National Congress.
 
• He helped form the Deccan Education Society and supported the creation of institutions like Fergusson College in Pune.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was associated with dance style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rukmini Devi Arundale was associated with the Indian classical dance form of Bharatnatyam: 
 
• She was a prominent revivalist of the original "Sadhir" style of Bharatanatyam, which was popular with temple dancers. 
 
• Founder of Kalakshetra Foundation
 
• She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Madras (now Chennai). 
 
• She was inspired by the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova and trained under her associates. 
 
• Other accomplishments
 
• She was also an animal rights activist, theosophist, and the first woman to be nominated for election to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• She received the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bharatanatyam
 
• This dance originated in Tamil Nadu and is based on the aesthetic ideas and performance outlined in the ancient treatise Natyashastra. It was originally a temple dance for women and is often used to express Hindu religious stories and devotions. 
 
• Kuchipudi
 
• This dance originated in Andhra Pradesh and is a dance-drama that combines Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressional dance), and Natya (drama). It evolved significantly due to the Bhakti movement that began in the 7th century AD. 
 
• Kathak
 
• This dance originated in Uttar Pradesh and is the main dance of northern India. The word Kathak means story, and the dancers narrate stories through their eyes and expressions. 
 
• Sattriya
 
• This dance refers to the body of dance and danced theater produced in Assam's sattras or monasteries during the sixteenth century. 
 
• Other classical dance forms of India include: Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, and Mohiniyattam.

questions.question: Watt is the unit of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The watt is the International System of Units (SI) unit of power.
 
• One watt is equal to one joule of work performed per second, or 1/746 horsepower.
 
• The symbol for watt is W.
 
• The watt is named after James Watt, an 18th-century Scottish inventor, mechanical engineer, and chemist.
 
• Watt's steam engine improved the Newcomen engine in 1776, which was a fundamental invention for the Industrial Revolution. 
 
• Other units of electric power include: Volt ampere, Kilowatt hour, Watt second, and Joule second. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance** is measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• **Energy** is measured in joules (J).
 
• **Momentum** is measured in kilogram-meters per second (kg·m/s).

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, Right against exploitation, prohibiting all forms of ________ and traffic in human beings.

__
 
• **According to the Indian Constitution**, the **Right against Exploitation prohibits all forms of forced labor and traffic in human beings**: 
 
• **Article 23**
 
• Prohibits trafficking in human beings, including forced labor, slavery, and exploitation.
 
• It also prohibits begar and other similar forms of forced labor. This article applies to both citizens and non-citizens, and protects against the state and private entities. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 24**

 
 
• **Prohibits the employment of children under the age of 14 in factories, mines, and other hazardous occupations.**
 
• **This article aims to protect the rights and well-being of children. **
 
• **The Right against Exploitation is a Fundamental Right that guarantees the dignity and freedom of a person.**
 
• **It also upholds the principles of equality, justice, and respect for human rights.**

questions.question: With respect to trade and industry, what is 'SCOMET'?

Framework for new trade policy in India

• **SCOMET s**tands for **Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment, and Technologies.**
 
• It's** India's National Export Control List, which regulates the export of dual-use items that can be used for both civilian and military purposes. **
 
• **The SCOMET list includes items such as munitions, nuclear-related items, software, and technology.**

questions.question: What is the function of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), with respect to monetary policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**issuing currency notes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is responsible for formulating and implementing monetary policy in India.
 
• **This includes: **
 
• **Regulating the issue of banknotes:** The RBI is the sole agency in India that issues banknotes. 
 
• **Managing the supply of money: **The RBI controls the supply of money in the economy. 
 
• **Maintaining price stability: **The RBI aims to maintain price stability while also considering growth. 
 
• **Securing monetary stability:** The RBI maintains reserves to secure monetary stability. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** RBI also has other functions, including:** Managing public debt, Acting as banker to the government and the banking system, Regulating bank reserves,
 
• **Supervising the banking and financial system, and Operating the credit and currency system. **
 
• RBI was set up on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission also called the Royal Commission in 1926.
 
• RBI Act was passed in the year - 1934
 
• RBI was established on 1st April 1935.
 
• RBI was nationalized on 1st January 1949.
 
• RBI issues all currency notes except one rupee.
 
• The signature of the RBI Governor on the notes is in English and Hindi.
 
• The currency notes except one rupee hold the signature of the RBI Governor.
 
• One rupee holds the signature of the Finance Secretary.

questions.question: In India, the Legal Services Authorities Act, __________ provides statutory status to the legal aid movement and it also provides for setting up of Legal Services Authorities at the Central, State and District levels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1987**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India,** the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 provides statutory status to the legal aid movement.**
 
• It **also mandates the establishment of Legal Services Authorities **at the Central, State, and District levels to ensure access to justice for all, particularly for marginalized and weaker sections of society.
 
• **This Act came into force on November 9, 1995, **
 
• **It is **instrumental in providing free legal aid and organizing Lok Adalats to resolve disputes efficiently and cost-effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The sections of the society as enlisted under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act are entitled to free legal services, they are :

 
• A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
 
• A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution
 
• A woman or a child
 
• A mentally ill or otherwise disabled person;
 
• A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; or
 
• An industrial workman; or
 
• In custody, including custody in a protective home within the meaning of clause (g) of Section 2 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956(104 of 1956
 
• In a juvenile home within the meaning of clause(j) of Section 2 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 (53 of 1986
 
• In a psychiatric hospital or psychiatric nursing home within the meaning of clause (g) of Section 2 of the Mental Health Act, 1987(14 of 1987)

questions.question: Who launched the 'Ayushman Bhava' campaign in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Droupadi Murmu**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The '**Ayushman Bhava' campaign was initiated by the Government of India in 2023 **to ensure the delivery of comprehensive healthcare services at the grassroots level.
 
• It **aligns with the broader vision of achieving universal health coverage under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme**.
 
• President Droupadi Murmu formally launched this campaign, emphasizing its significance in improving healthcare access and quality, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The campaign focuses on**:

• Seva Pakhwada (Service Fortnight) - Encouraging healthcare awareness and enrollment activities.
 
• Gram Panchayat Health Melas - Organized at the village level to promote health and wellness.
 
• By involving local administrations, healthcare providers, and communities, the initiative seeks to bring health services closer to people, ensuring no one is left behind.​

questions.question: Which one is not the cause of Poverty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slow growth of the the Population**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Slow growth of populatio**n is not a cause of poverty. 
 
• **Some causes of poverty include:**
 
• **Unemployment:** Individuals and communities suffer poverty when they don't have money from employment. 
 
• **Unequal distribution of resources:** Concentration of land ownership is one example of this. 
 
• **Overpopulation:** This can tax limited resources and cause environmental degradation. 
 
• **Lack of access to basic needs**: This includes access to clean water, food, shelter, and healthcare. 
 
• **Gender discrimination: **This can be a cause of poverty. 
 
• **Poverty trap:** This is when individuals remain in low-income jobs and are unable to escape. 
 
• Poverty can lead to health problems, poor sanitation, lack of education, and lack of efficient human resources for the economy.
